narrative:
Your school asked a model to estimate each student’s chance of failing the final year, and for you that estimate is 13%. This means that among 100 students with a profile like yours, about 13 would not finish the year, while 87 would pass. Passing is therefore the more likely outcome, but the school considers a 13% risk too high to ignore, and that is why you must take remedial courses as a safeguard.

What led to this requirement? The model weighed many aspects of your situation, but three stood out most clearly. The strongest factor is that you have never failed a year before. This works in your favor, because students who have never repeated a grade are far less likely to fail now; your clean record is a solid foundation. The second most influential factor is your desire to continue into higher education. This ambition lowers your risk considerably, and indeed nearly every student who passed in the data shared it. The third is your weekend alcohol consumption
